DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 27 S. 2021 17 February 2021 HON. ANTHONY A. DAYONDON OIC, Office of the Mayor Municipality of Tabina, Zamboanga del Sur Dear Hon. Dayondon: This has reference to the attached Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 060-2019, dated 13 December 2019, which states that Alfredo A. Mamintas, representative of the Indigenous People, is thereby expelled from the Sangguniang Bayan as the legitimate representative of the Indigenous People of Tabina, Zamboanga del Sur. Pursuant to the aforesaid SB Resolution, IP representative Alfredo Mamintas failed to attend any sessions of the Sanggunian since the conduct of their first session, which was first held on 01 July 2019 until 09 December 2019. Thus, incurring an accumulated absences of nineteen (19) sangunian sessions. By reason thereof, the Indigenous People of Tabina, Zamboanga del Sur issued a Manifesto, duly signed and thumb marked by two hundred fifty (250) Subanen Leaders and Certification of the Tabina Indigenous Peoples Council of Leaders to the effect that IP representative Alfredo Mamintas is no longer the duly authorized representative of the Indigenous People in the Sangguniang Bayan of Tabina, on the ground of loss of confidence that he can effectively represent them. As a result thereof, Mr. Elmer B. Mamintas was certified by the IPs as their new representative to the sanggunian. In the interim, Alfredo Mamintas chanced upon Mayor Tirsendo C. Poloyapoy who encouraged him to present justification relative to his absences and present the same to the IPs for the latter's consideration. In the meantime however, pending the submission and presentation by Alfredo Mamintas of the aforesaid justification, Mayor Poloyapoy offered Elmer B. Mamintas the position of Deputy Mayor for Subanen Tribe, to which the latter accepted. Meanwhile, on 25 September 2019, Mayor Poloyapoy issued Memorandum Order No. 041-09-25-2019 which orders the Municipal

Treasury Division and Municipal Accounting Division to hold the salary of Alfredo Mamintas effective September 2019 and thereafter, due to the latter's abandonment of his position by not reporting and attending legislative sessions. Nonetheless, despite said directive, the Sangguniang Bayan learned that Alfredo Mamintas was able to receive his salaries for the months of September to November 2019. Hence, the following issues: 1. Whether or Not a self-imposed Acting Mayor can revoke a hold- salary order of a duly elected Municipal Mayor 2. Whether or Not an Indigenous People's Representative already replaced by the Indigenous People still has qualification and illegibility to represent the Indigenous People 3. Whether or Not the Municipal Accountant and the Acting Municipal Treasurer who conspired in the release of the salaries have incurred criminal and administrative liabilities. On the first issue, we regret to inform you that the facts provided and circumstances surrounding the same are insufficient for us to conclude a logical answer. In fact, it was not mentioned who is the supposed "self- imposed Acting Mayor and the revocation of the hold-salary order was not even discussed in detail. With respect to the second issue, we are of the understanding and interpretation that the question should have been in this wise: Whether or Not an IP representative, who was replaced by the IPs, can still represent the IPs thereafter. Pertinent to the foregoing is the National Commission on Indigenous People (NCIP) Administrative Order No. 03, Series of 20181, specifically Section 8(A), 9, 10, and 11 thereof, which provide: "Section 8. Qualifications. The following shall be the minimum requirements for one to qualify as IPMR: A. General Requirements. The selected IPMR must be: I. A bonafide member of the Indigenous Peoples community he/she seeks to represent, supported by a certification from his/her IPs; 2. Able to read and write; 3. Physically, mentally and morally fit; I Revised National Guidelines for the Mandatory Representation of Indigenous Peoples in Local Legislative Councils and Policy-Making Bodies

4. A natural born Filipino citizen; 5. At least 18 years of age on the date of assumption; 6. Such other qualifications that the community may include in their local guidelines. Section 9. Disqualifications. The following circumstances shall disqualify an aspiring PMR from selection: a. b. c. d. e. f. g. h. i. j. k. Section Found guilty by the IPs of violating their customs and traditions; Sentenced by final judgment for an offense involving moral turpitude or for an offense punishable by imprisonment of one (1) year or more, within two (2) years after serving sentence; Removed from office as a result of administrative case; Convicted by final judgment for violating the oath of allegiance to the Republic of the Philippines; Fugitive from justice; Should not have held any office in the Government one year prior to the selection process; Affiliation to any political party or soliciting support from politicians; Supporter of any activity prejudicial to the interest of the Iccsnps; Insane or feeble-minded based on the findings of competent authorities; Losing candidate to any immediately preceding national or local election; Such other disqualifications as the community mav impose in their local guidelines. IO. Local Guidelines. Each community shall formulate its guidelines for the selection of their IPMR in consonance with their customary laws. The local guidelines must at least contain the following: a. b. c. d. e. f. g. h. i. Definition of terms; of Composition Council Leaders/Elders/lndigenous Political Structure; Qualifications of selectors and mode of replacing the selectors; Selection process which identify representation levels, e.g. Barangays, Municipality, City, Provinces, Regions, National, Institutions and Public Utilities; Selection in policy making bodies; Re-Selection Process: Qualifications: Disgualifications; Community confirmation and nomination;

j. k. I. m. n. o. p. q. r. s. t. Section Vacancy: Disciplinary action; Grounds for disciplinary action; Term of office Term rotation, if applicable; Removal processes: Grievance and redress mechanism; Hold-over capacity; Special provisions, if any; Amendment; and Effectivity clause. II. Selection and Assumption to Office. The selection process shall be in accordance with their local quidelines that is consistent with their customary laws. (Emphasis Supplied) It is indisputable that representation of Indigenous Cultural Communities/lndigenous Peoples (ICCs/lPs) in the local sanggunian is mandatory pursuant to Republic Act No. 8371, otherwise known as the "Indigenous People Rights Act of 1991". Said law provides that ICCs/lPs have the right to participate fully, if they so choose, at all levels of decision- making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through procedures determined by them as well as to maintain and develop their own indigenous political structures. Moreover, Section 6, Rule IV of the Implementing Rules and Regulations thereof mandates that ICCs/lPs shall be provided mandatory representation in all policy making bodies in local sanggunians. Clearly, based from the foregoing, although representation of IPs is mandatory, the selection, qualification, disqualification, and removal of their representative shall be in accordance with the local guidelines established by them (IPs) in their community. Hence, in reply to the second issue, the possible subsequent representation of Alfredo Mamintas as representative of IPs, after he has been removed and replaced by the IPs, would depend in the local guidelines issued by the concerned community, subject however to the process as provided under NCIP Administrative Order No. ()3, s. 2018. This Department had been consistent in its opinion2 that the ICC/IP representative to the local sanggunian shall be selected in accordance with the Local Guideline duly adopted and promulgated by the ICCs/lPs themselves; the latter are given a wide latitude of decision-making with respect to selecting who will be their representative. 2 DILG Opinion No. 20, s. 2011, dated May 31, 2011

Anent the third issue regarding the possible criminal and administrative liabilities of the Municipal Accountant and Municipal Treasurer, we are of the view that the same is justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law. Therefore, we are inhibited to act on the same. Nonetheless, for purposes of discussion, may we invite your attention to Sections 443(a), 470(b) and last paragraph of Section 474(a) of Republic Act 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), in relation to Section 30 of Executive Order No, 292, the pertinent provisions of which state: "SECTION 443. Officials of the Municipal Government. (b) There shall be in each municipality a municipal mayor xxx, municipal treasurer, municipal assessor, municipal accountant, municipal budget officer, xxx SECTION 470 (a) The treasurer shall be appointed by the Secretary of Finance from a list of three (3) ranking eligible recomendees of the governor or mayor, as the case may be, subject to civil service laws, rules and regulations. (b) The treasurer shall be under the administrative supervision of the governor or mayor, as the case may be, to whom he shall report regularly on the tax collection efforts in the local government unit. SECTION 474. The appointment of an accountant is mandatory for the provincial, city and municipal governments" "SECTION 30. Authority to Appoint and Discipline.—The head of bureau or office shall appoint personnel to all positions in his bureau or office, in accordance with law. In the case of the line bureau or office, the head shall also appoint the second level personnel of the regional offices, unless such power has been delegated. He shall have the authority to discipline employees in accordance with the Civil Service Law." (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the foregoing, appointment of municipal treasurer and municipal accountant are mandatory in municipalities. Likewise, it is clear that the local chief executive, in this case, the Municipal Mayor, has the power to appoint the municipal accountant. However, with respect to the appointment of municipal treasurer, Section 470(a) of the LGC in relation to Article 122(b)(1) of its Implementing Rules and Regulations, find application. It is provided therein that the Secretary of Finance shall have the power to appoint municipal treasurers, subject however, to the administrative supervision of the governor or mayor, as the case may be.

Relatedly, the local chief executive may discipline appointive local officials and employees pursuant to Sections 83, 84, 86 and 87 of the LGC, through a person or committee established for that purpose. The pertinent provisions of the law provide: "Sec. 83. Grievance Procedure- In every local government unit, the local chief executive shall establish a procedure to inquire into, act upon, resolve or settle complaints and grievances presented by local government employees. Sec. 84. Administrative Discipline- Investigation and adjudication of administrative complaints against appointive local officials and employees as well as their suspension and removal shall be in accordance with the civil service laws and rules and other pertinent laws. The results of such administrative investigations shall be reponed to the Civil Service Commission. Section 86. Administrative Investigation In any local government unit, administrative investigation may. be conducted by a person or a committee duly authorized bv the local chief executive. Said person or committee shall conduct hearings on the cases brought against appointive local officials or employees xxx. The administrative cases herein mentioned shall be decided within ninety (90) days from the time the respondent is formally notified of the charges. Sec. 87. Disciplinary Jurisdiction- Except as otherwise provided by law, the local chief executive may impose the penalty of removal from service, demotion in rank, suspension for not more than one (1) year without pay, fine in an amount not exceeding six (6) months' salary, or reprimand and otherwise discipline subordinate officials and employees under his jurisdiction. If the penalty imposed is suspension without pay for not more than thirty (30) days, his decision shall be final. If the penalty imposed is heavier than suspension of thirty (30) days, the decision shall be appealable to the Civil Service Commission, which shall decide the appeal within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof." (Emphasis Ours) In this regard, the phrase "person or committee" as used in Section 86 of the LGC refers only to person/s or individual/s or group thereof who are employees of the local government unit, over which the City Mayor, as in this case, exercises administrative authority or disciplinary powers as Local Chief Executive. Thus, the Municipal Mayor has the power to discipline appointed officials and employees of the local government unit, such as the

municipal accountant. The same, however, is different with respect to the discipline of municipal treasurers. This Department, in DILG Legal Opinion No. 19, Series of 2019 dated 08 February 2010, posits, that it is within the power of Secretary of Finance to appoint treasurers. Corollary thereto, it is within Secretary of Finance's power to terminate said designation. Hence, in actions involving municipal treasurers, the municipal mayor can merely recommend for the relief, recall and designation of a municipal treasurer. It should be noted that pursuant to Section 444(b)(x) of the LGC, the Mayor's power over the said municipal treasurer is merely supervisory. The pertinent provision reads: "Ensure that all executive officials and employees of the municipality faithfully discharge their duties and functions as provided by law and this Code, and cause to be instituted administrative and judicial proceedings against any official or employee of the municipality who may have committed an offense in the performance of his official duties. " To reiterate, it is the municipal mayor who has disciplinary authority over municipal accountants, and exercises supervisory authority over municipal treasurers. On the other hand, with respect to municipal treasurer, it is the Secretary of Finance who has the power to appoint and terminate. Necessarily, the Secretary of Finance likewise has disciplinary power over treasurers. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, Authority of the Secretary: INGAN, CESO Ill tary for Local Government o LegaV91 Copy Furnished: DIRECTOR PAISAL O. ABUTAZIL Regional Director, DILG-Region IX AT D, Bldg., F.S.
